title: Paperclip on‑Prem Burst Replay & Runbook
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures results from the Paperclip Analytics on-prem POC burst replay and a pragmatic runbook for keeping tail latency bounded during microbursts. We ran a replay of production traces (10h window) against an on-prem rack with two H100 nodes (2x H100, 80GB) under Redwood runtime v2.14 and compared model variants and quantization settings. Key takeaway: with modest runtime tweaks (continuous batching enabled, reduce max_batch_latency_ms, KV cache warmup) we can meet a 150ms p95 target for short (<=2s) responses at moderate QPS, and recover gracefully from sustained microbursts with <2x cost uplift compared to the steady state.

POC goals:
- Validate on-prem latency/throughput for Paperclip's real traffic replay (mixed small/medium prompts)
- Surface configurations that control p95/p99 tails during microbursts
- Provide a runbook for productionization (warmup, autoscale triggers, routing) and a rough cost delta vs hosted inference

Test matrix and environment:
- Hardware: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB (single rack), 64 vCPU frontend nodes for load generation separated from serving hosts
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime v2.14 (build 2.14.3), model server pinned to model version: rw-7b-v1.3 (fp16), and rw-7b-q4_0 (quantized 4-bit) for comparison
- Serving config (baseline): continuous_batching=true, max_batch_size=64, max_batch_latency_ms=20, kv_cache=true, prefix_cache=enabled, concurrency_per_gpu=4
- Workloads: production trace replay (10h window) with realistic inter-arrival, mixed prompt lengths (median prompt 24 tokens, median completion length targeted 128 tokens), microburst patterns (sudden spikes to 2500 qps sustained for 15s, every ~6 minutes)
- Load tools: custom replay harness built on top of k6 + custom token-accurate generators; telemetry collected into Grafana/Prometheus (links in linked_artifacts)

Observations (baseline fp16 model):
- Steady-state (300 qps): p50=22ms, p95=58ms, p99=140ms, GPU util ~32% (per GPU), tokens/sec ~41k
- Microbursts (peak 2500 qps, 15s): p50=28ms, p95=370ms, p99=1120ms. Tail spikes align with cold KV/cache misses and queueing during in-progress large batches.
- Coldstart-ish behavior when long idle periods (>20m) precede bursts — initial 60–90s of higher p99 (up to 2.4s) as caches warm and batching stabilizes

Quantized model (rw-7b-q4_0):
- Steady-state (300 qps): p50=18ms, p95=45ms, p99=120ms, GPU util ~28%, tokens/sec ~56k
- Microbursts (2500 qps): p95=310ms, p99=980ms — better tail but still shows similar pattern; quantization helps throughput and baseline latency but not tail sources (queueing/KV misses)

Cost sketch (on‑prem vs hosted):
- Measured token rate during steady-state ~50k tokens/sec across the rack. Using Paperclip's expected monthly tokens (100M tokens/day), this translates to ~3 racks-month sustained capacity if we keep 30% headroom for bursts.
- Incremental cost for burst tolerance (autoscale buffers, spare capacity): ~+45% CAPEX/OPEX depending on autoscale policy. Compared to Redwood hosted (approx pricing estimate linked in Confluence), paperclip on-prem steady-state cost baseline is roughly comparable for committed workloads, but on-prem requires ops overhead and a 0.35–0.6x higher cost during peak-heavy months due to buffer capacity. (Numbers intentionally coarse for planning).

Root causes for tail latency:
- Queueing: with max_batch_latency_ms=20, large microbursts build big batches that take longer to execute; while batching helps throughput, it raises latency for individual requests when queues are long.
- KV/prefix cache cold misses: when bursts are not preceded by warm traffic, first few requests miss caches leading to higher model execution and I/O.
- Scheduling jitter across GPUs: when concurrency_per_gpu is low and many small requests arrive, we observe scheduling hotspots where a small subset of GPUs receive disproportionate load for brief windows.

Config experiments and results:
1) Reduce max_batch_latency_ms to 8ms, increase max_batch_size to 96, continuous_batching=true:
   - p95 during bursts improved from 370ms -> 220ms, p99 from 1120ms -> 540ms, but GPU utilization increases and tokens/sec drops slightly during sustained peaks (due to smaller batching windows).
2) Enable aggressive KV warmup: synthetic warmup every 4 minutes during low traffic windows (short prefix replays):
   - Eliminated the first-60s high p99 behavior in 90% of replays; tail reduced by ~18% on average during burst start.
3) Adjust routing: route >=95th percentile request size to dedicated pool with higher concurrency_per_gpu=8 and smaller batch latency:
   - Reduced p99 for large completions by ~30% during bursts, minimal impact on cost since large completions are <12% of traffic.

Recommendations / runbook (practical steps for Paperclip):
- Immediate (week 0–2):
  1. Deploy runtime config changes: set max_batch_latency_ms=8, max_batch_size=96, continuous_batching=true on canary pool.
  2. Implement KV warmup job in Cron to replay top-200 prefixes every 4–6 minutes during low traffic hours.
  3. Introduce routing rule: requests with expected completion >256 tokens -> dedicated high-concurrency lane (concurrency_per_gpu=8).
  4. Add surge alarm: when QPS > 1.2x steady-state for 30s, spin up a spare GPU node (policy: keep for min 2 minutes) and notify oncall channel.

- Medium term (2–8 weeks):
  1. Pilot quantized RW model (rw-7b-q4_0) in dedicated lane for cost-sensitive workloads and measure quality regression across eval set (links to eval suite in Confluence).
  2. Add a lightweight synthetic health probe that mimics a small prefix every 60s to maintain cache heat.
  3. Tune autoscaler: reduce scale-up latency by pre-warming images and keep a fractional spare capacity (10–15%).

- Longer term (quarter):
  1. Explore hybrid routing: daytime traffic to dedicated low-latency pools, night to cost-optimized pooled capacity.
  2. Evaluate model distillation/shorter completion paths for 80% of intents to materially reduce tokens per session and cost.

Checklist for engineers (copyable):
- [ ] Apply runtime change to canary pool: max_batch_latency_ms=8, max_batch_size=96
- [ ] Add cron KV warmup job (script: scripts/kv-warmup-replay.sh, see linked GitHub)
- [ ] Create routing policy in Console: route completion_size>256 -> pool-paperclip-large
- [ ] Add alert: QPS surge >1.2x steady for 30s -> autoscale up (retain for 2 minutes) + Slack notify
- [ ] Run quantized model A/B for 2 weeks using eval prompt set 'paperclip-quality-2028-01'

Open questions / risks:
- Model quality for rw-7b-q4_0: preliminary eval shows small hallucination spike on multi-step prompts; Paperclip product team needs to sign off.
- Ops ownership for on-prem warmup cron job (who owns it? Paperclip infra or Redwood SRE runbook?).
- Exact autoscale policy tuning will materially affect cost; we recommend a short (2–4 week) observability-driven tuning period before committing to static capacity contracts.

Appendix: relevant commands and quick reproducer
- Run replay harness (k6): k6 run --vus 200 --duration 15s --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086 scripts/paperclip-replay.js
- Warmup script (example): ./scripts/kv-warmup-replay.sh --prefix-list top200 --target http://realtime.paperclip.local/api/generate --concurrency 8
- Profiling snippet (on host): sudo nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5; watch for GPU utilization spikes, mem utilization

Notes to self / meeting follow-ups:
- Share canary pool config with Paperclip infra and schedule 30m alignment call (owner: Marco Chen).
- Add a KPI dashboard tile: "burst p95 (15s windows)" and baseline it for 4 week observation.

This doc is a working artifact — expect small numbers refinement after the next replay run on 2028-01-18. See linked artifacts for raw traces and dashboards.
